title: Which Ai models do you prefer for Game Dev?
author: UbiNax
selftext:
Hey all, 

I'm wondering what AI models everyone prefer for Game Dev, and why do you prefer them over others?

For me I've recently only really been using OpenAI models, more specifically GPT6 Astra and 6.1 Sol.

But while I like the results of Astra, I can't really deal with the rate it burns usage/tokens, I can pretty much go through a 100$ weekly within a day... and while I love the efficiency of 6.1 sol, I also feel like it falls short in some areas.

So what do you all use and why? :)

Share your experiences. <3

Br

replies.author: TheBigQuestion354
replies.body: Personally I still prefer Fable but only as the designer. I give it a bigger task/new system then tell it to spin up as many Opus builders as it needs and it just needs to direct them/be the architect.

replies.author: Specialist_Aerie_175
replies.body: Fable yaps alot, reminds me of opus 5.0, personally i cant stand that style of communication so i use opus 5.5 for everything, i just tweak the effort level depending on the task.

replies.author: MotivatedforGames
replies.body: I'm using Astra. Its handled everything ivr thrown at it

comments.author: TheBigQuestion354
comments.body: Also Astra is still good at some stuff. It is way better at “one shotting” a good looking map then use Opus to refine the details. I have 3 max Claude plans and one $100 GPT plan though so it’s clearly still the laggard.

comments.author: Limp_Bus3865
comments.body: Claude is best at everything. Always has been I have no idea why anyone would use codex

replies.author: Qottonmouth
replies.body: Sounds like you haven't tried Codex tbh

replies.author: Limp_Bus3865
replies.body: I did. Codex is great at convincing you that it knows how to write code well, because things usually work good enough, but it soon falls apart, claude is much better and write better code

replies.author: Qottonmouth
replies.body: When does its mistakes "fall apart"?

comments.author: Ok-Control-5800
comments.body: Anthropic is much too expensive to use it as solo dev or hobby dev. It had the worst token for dollar output you can get.

replies.author: zoopesh
replies.body: I was wasting cheap tokens and getting no work done. Cheap doesn't mean better if you end up spending more to get the same work done

replies.author: Ok-Control-5800
replies.body:
I agree, but it depends on your project. You won’t need a frontier model for everything and if you are good at prompting Sol6.1 would do it too.   
Remember what we worked with 6 month ago.

replies.author: random_boss
replies.body: 6 months ago I wasn’t getting serious work done the way I am now. Yes, they would output functioning code, but the cracks would always start to show. On the 5x plan I can work all week and only until recently did the “2 steps forward 3 steps back” really go away. Everything before that was either practice or required me to intervene heavily or just shut projects down.

replies.author: Arya_the_Gamer
replies.body: Why did you even get downvoted for saying the right thing? Game development is an iterative process, as a result you'll end up having to do a lot of back and forth between prompts to get things done the way you want it to be, which means a token black hole for fine tuning a mechanic or fixing some bugs.

comments.author: JDad67
comments.body: Claude Opus 5.5.  No question to me.

comments.author: M4xs0n
comments.body: Codex. Astra before 6.1 Sol released. Now you can use Sol for almost everything and its insane. Also, everyone recommends Claude. I get it, its good and way better for asset creation like 3d Models etc. but the 5 hour limit is a joke. I am not sure if the limit gets higher with the $100 plan but if not then it‘s way better to use Codex for coding and only if it doesn’t get the Job done, you could use Opus. Especially for visual tasks. You can let GPT-6.1 Sol run for 12 Hours straight or even more on multiple tasks and projects and it just performs. Also the random resets of your usage here in there are very nice

replies.author: Qottonmouth
replies.body: Yoo Sol 6.1 Extra High represent! I can't believe it doesn't use resources. I'm all here like: "you sure you don't want more of those weekly credits?" and never reaching the 5h limit until they already have reset

replies.author: M4xs0n
replies.body: Its absolutely insane. A better deal than anything else 😂

replies.author: PeanutSilent884
replies.body: I don't think many people ever hit the five hour limit anymore, if you continuously hit the five hour your weekly would be gone in two days so it's almost moot

replies.author: M4xs0n
replies.body: I do all the time. In a simple daily task it wouldn‘t make sense, sure. But what are people doing then. Especially when you Build Systems and mechanics you would use up all of the 5 Hour limit crazy fast

replies.author: random_boss
replies.body:
I have a 5x plan and have never hit the 5 hour limit. I use an opus orchestrator with mostly opus planners and implementers, usually with two lanes running simultaneously. OP is right, if you hit the 5hr limit your weekly would be gone in like 2 days. 

Incidentally to this thread when I also had a codex pro sub I would regularly burn through the entire weekly quota in one session.

replies.author: UbiNax
replies.body:
Yeah that is my issue at the moment with 5x Codex pro sub, if I run GPT-6 Astra High, I can run through my weekly in a single day.
So while the 6Astra is great in many ways, it is rough if you want to use your subscription for the entire week..
6.1 sol is great in many ways, but you can also feel, that it is still not Astra.. so when you run into an issue that you have a hard time solving, that you gotta go "burn" some tokens on the Astra model..
I kinda wish they had a middle ground to 6Astra and 6.1Sol.. 
(Astra costs 5 times as much as 6.1Sol.)
That is where Oppus 5.5 is compelling, since it does seem to have better results than 6.1Sol, in many aspects.. but is also "only" twice as expensive.. and not 5 times as much, as Astra.

replies.author: SeasonedAdManager
replies.body: I never hit the 5 hour limit on my team plan with lots of dev work going in. I think I struggle to hit 50% on my personal $200 plans.

replies.author: M4xs0n
replies.body: So it‘s linked to the plan you pay for I assume? Well then a higher plan would make more sense than the normal one

comments.author: drallcom3
comments.body: GLM Flash is nice for most parts. You only need Opus etc for the difficult tasks, like Blender.

comments.author: geddy
comments.body: Sonnet 5 medium effort lol, Opus is great but my tokens last forever and I get exactly what I want out of Sonnet!

replies.author: sh0cki
replies.body:
I hope you mean Sonnet 5.5, cause that one is on fire and super cheap.  
But with the recent pricing drop for Opus 5.5, I default to it for both planning and coding on my Max20.  
Working on few projects in parallel and it is still covering it.

replies.author: geddy
replies.body: Oh yes, I do mean 5.5, thanks. I will update. Perhaps I'll try Opus for the rest of the week and see if I like it more.

replies.author: random_boss
replies.body: Man I don’t know how you guys are using sonnet. I ask my orchestrator to score every agent before we decide to bring it in. Sonnet was given multiple tasks and never received a passing grade, so it doesn’t get used in the rotation.

comments.author: SeasonedAdManager
comments.body: Opus 5.5 coordinating Sonnet for easy stuff and Opus for harder stuff. Astra for adversarial reviews. A final pass with Opus for a counter review.

comments.author: Efficient_Cup947
comments.body:
Using cursor IDE with 20 dollar pro plan . Generally I go for grok 4.6 high/medium for unity coding . But switch to grok 4.7 for blender mcp rigging and animation . 
1 normal prompt cost around 1-2 million tokens. If u give very large prompt like code a whole level with asset generation , it will take 10 million tokens . And the monthly limit is 700 million tokens for grok 4.6 , 450 million tokens for grok 4.7 . So I use it wisely to not hit limit at month end . 


I don't care if someone would comment grok is useless or not . I have used it and grok is good , less than claude models in , but grok has gives 700 million tokens, which is cheap
